feedback: The confession follows the evidence available before voting: Reed's sample, access to the waiting glass, knowledge of original contents, and visibly false description of the press edit all pointed in the same direction. Saying explicitly that he put poison into the glass confirms the inference rather than supplying a missing external clue. Chip and Elle's readings give satisfying separate purposes to their lies without undoing the evidence. Reed's final concern with controlling the published version fits his scholarly insecurity and his earlier caption work. The closing line about Claire is emotionally sharper than a procedural recap. The motive remains somewhat broad professional panic, but the confession feels earned and suitably personal.
